$schema_note: Read by scripts/check-budgets.ts against dist/.vite/manifest.json. Licensing: budgets.json.license (REUSE sidecar; JSON admits no comment syntax).
rationale: D13 — budgets are tests. 'Sub-second on a mine-site laptop' is a number or it is marketing. Every threshold below is gzip of the transferred JavaScript and CSS closure, not raw bytes, because gzip is what the wire carries.

budgets.title: Evidentiary shell (entry chunk + its static import closure + CSS)
budgets.why: The refusal must paint before a supervisor decides the screen is broken. This is the only weight on the critical path; every feature surface is a lazy chunk.

budgets.title: Lazy 3D chunk (the MEMORY-register ancestry walk)
budgets.why: The one dimensional surface. It is loaded only after a refusal has been shown, only on a machine that passed the capability probe, and it is cut ladder item 1 — so its absence is legal and is NOT a budget failure.
budgets.absent_note: render3d/ is not present in this build. BUILD_PLAN §10.2 cut 1 has either been taken or the surface has not landed yet. The ribbon carries every fact the walk does (ui.md §1.3), so this is a texture loss, not a claim loss.

forbidden_in_entry.why: MEMORY-register libraries must never reach the evidentiary shell. If three.js is statically reachable from the entry chunk, the lazy boundary has been broken and every machine pays for a surface most of them will never render.
